correctness.rationale: For displacement d, at least r+1 voters incur h-over-w Borda gap at least d and at most r can counter with gap no more than m-1. A unique Borda winner requires (r+1)d<r(m-1). The two-ballot construction with a=1+floor((m-1)/(r+1)) gives exact score differences (r+1)a-y>0 versus every more extreme candidate and unanimous preferences over less extreme candidates; thereby exact sharpness for all m>=2, r>=1. The median premise is independently proved. The verifier exhaustively examines thirteen finite combinations and tests 1960 constructions, while the general claim rests on the analytical argument.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic queries and relevant primary comparisons found prior qualitative finite-agenda disagreement and continuous-domain coincidence but not a proof of the sharp maximal index displacement D(m,r), attained by two ballot types for every odd electorate and agenda size. One highly relevant older primary study was inspected in author-posted full text, including all main theorems and boundary discussion. The inspected 2025 study covers expected winners under stochastic ballot cultures instead of worst-case deterministic profiles. Residual priority risk remains.
residual_risks: An earlier exact finite-agenda maximum could have been published using a different name such as Condorcet–Borda spectrum, ideological compromise diameter, or median displacement; searches do not prove uniqueness.
The 1948 original publisher manuscript was not readable in full, although its required median-premise statement and proof are independently established.

value.rationale: This exact maximal ideological-axis disagreement between majority rule and Borda is a motivated natural invariant of the finite-agenda spatial voting model, not an arbitrary small-case tally. The complete closed formula gives a sharp two-parameter extremal law and the first possible electorate size (2m-1) for distance m-2. It quantitatively resolves how far the finite-agenda Borda outcome can move despite common single-peaked preferences; Feld–Grofman explicitly motivate finite vs continuous agenda effects, but do not supply this bound. Its elementary proof does not reduce the relevance of the exact extremal characterization. The result does not claim a downstream theorem or practical forecast.
